messages:
Aisha (CEO): Thanks everyone — opening this All-Hands Q&A thread. Drop questions about mission, positioning, market, competitors, or follow-ups from today's talk and we'll answer over the next hour. Recording + notes will be posted here after. :sparkles:

Marco (CTO): I'll be jumping in on infra/technical positioning questions. Also posting a short note about Dedicated vs Private after the session.

Sam (eng): Quick one — how should engineers pitch Redwood vs "managed endpoints" from the big clouds? What's the single-sentence differentiation we want folks to use?

Aisha (CEO): Short answer: "We offer a production-first inference runtime that makes LLMs predictable and economical across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments." Emphasize predictable latency, clear unit economics, and same APIs across modes.

Taylor (sales): Follow-up — for enterprise buyers worried about lock-in, what's our messaging on portability?

Dana (VP Product): Portability is core: customers can pin model versions and use our private deployment when they need isolation. We also publish model compatibility notes and migration guides.

Sam (eng): On the technical side — will we prioritize throughput or single-request latency for Dedicated? Customers ask both.

Marco (CTO): We design policies per customer SLA: Dedicated lets you choose throughput-optimized pools vs low-latency pools. Runtime supports continuous batching plus per-route latency SLOs.

Taylor (sales): Competitors question: How do we position vs XCloudAI and FastServe? Need two bullet points to share with prospects.

Aisha (CEO): Two bullets: 1) Unified runtime + ops primitives across hosted/dedicated/private (so you don't rebuild infra as you scale). 2) Cost-aware controls (batching, KV/prefix cache, quantization recommendations) that actually move the needle on per-token costs.

Sam (eng): Any plan to publish head-to-head cost/latency benchmarks? Reps want data. :eyes:

Dana (VP Product): Yes — we'll ship a reproducible benchmark suite (traffic-shaped scenarios) next quarter and maintain a public dashboard. We'll include guidance on common config knobs and expected savings.

RecordingBot: Recording started 1750001300

Marco (CTO): One more technical point: our fallback policies are a differentiator — auto-route to quantized or smaller model when capacity is constrained while preserving response shape. Example config snippet:```
rollout: {
  canary: 0.1,
  fallback: ["mpt-7b-quant", "llama-2-13b-q4"],
  target_latency_ms: 200
}
```

Sam (eng): Thanks — last question from me: how aggressively are we investing in model support vs runtime features?

Aisha (CEO): Both, but with priority: runtime & ops > model packaging. We onboard models only to the extent they prove useful for customer workloads; the core moat is the serving/observability stack.

Taylor (sales): On pricing — are we moving to simpler packaging? Reps get pushback on per-token complexity with embeddings vs generation.

Dana (VP Product): We're experimenting with simplified bundles for common usage patterns (e.g., embed-heavy vs generate-heavy). No final decision yet — we'll pilot with a subset of customers.

Sam (eng): How should teams ask for a feature change on rollouts or routing?

Marco (CTO): File an RFC in the #eng-platform backlog and tag me. Small changes can be shipped as config options; bigger ones start as design docs.

Taylor (sales): Any recommended collateral for Q2 field enablement?

Dana (VP Product): We'll publish a short playbook: "How to sell Redwood against cloud endpoints" and a one-pager on Dedicated vs Private. Expect drafts in two weeks.

Aisha (CEO): Thanks for the great questions. We'll compile answers and link the recording + slides. If you need to escalate something sensitive (legal/security), DM me or send to security@redwood.inference. :sparkles: :thumbsup:

Sam (eng): Appreciate it — very helpful.

Taylor (sales): :raised_hands: good session — please ping when the playbook is live.

Marco (CTO): Posting a follow-up note to #eng-runtime with a short architecture diagram and the fallback config examples in 15m.

Aisha (CEO): We'll close this thread in an hour after we attach notes. Thanks all!
